title: Parcelled Stream Frames: SDK ergonomics & experiments
body:
Purpose:
This sketch explores an alternative streaming shape we prototyped in a small lab: "Parcelled stream frames" (short: parcels). The idea: instead of one continuous token stream or rigid frame boundary, responses are emitted as semantically coherent "parcels" that can be independently acknowledged, patched, or rolled back by the client and server. This doc captures the API experiment, SDK ergonomics we tried, tradeoffs, and an outcomes log.

Why we tried this:
- Observed pain: complex tool-calling flows often require partial side-effects (e.g., create-draft -> attach-metadata -> finalize). Developers want per-action acknowledgment and the ability to rewind or reissue later frames without re-running entire generation.
- Goal: give SDKs an ergonomic primitive that maps to common app flows (preview, commit, speculative-tool-call, local-edit).

High-level primitive:
- Parcel: a discrete output unit with: id (client-visible), ordinal (monotonic for session), type (narrative|action|schema|attachment), soft-score (confidence/quality hint).
- Parcel stream: an ordered sequence of parcels. Parcels may be flagged as tentative or committed. Tentative parcels are best-effort. Committed parcels are durable and recorded in session state.

Example minimal HTTP/WS shape (informal):
- Start call: POST /v1/responses?session=xyz -> returns call_id, initial_session_state
- Server pushes: {parcel_id, ordinal, type, payload, tentative:true, meta:{latency_ms, model_revision}}
- Client can ACK or NACK parcel: POST /v1/calls/{call_id}/ack {parcel_id, ack: true|false, decision_reason}
- Server may later send an update parcel with same parcel_id and tentative:false to indicate commit or replacement.

Tool-calling coordination pattern:
- When an action-parcel triggers a tool (e.g., execute-query), the parcel includes a tool_hint block (tool_name, input_preview). SDK auto-batches tool calls unless developer opts out.
- Parcel A (tentative) -> SDK auto-invokes tool stub locally (simulate) -> UI shows preview -> developer clicks commit -> SDK sends ack to server -> server may escalate tentative -> committed and emit final parcel.

SDK ergonomics notes (lessons from lab):
- API surface: we experimented with two levels: low-level parcel stream events and a high-level SessionBuilder. Low-level gives maximum control but is noisy. SessionBuilder made common flows (preview -> commit) 6x fewer lines in user code.
- Backpressure: defining ordinal + optional size_hint lets SDK politely pause parsing to avoid UI floods on mobile.
- Idempotency: parcel IDs are stable across retries; ACKs include client_nonce to defend against double-commit.
- Offline-first: SDK keeps a local ledger of tentative parcels; on reconnect it reconciles ACKs. This maps well to offline editing apps.

Developer ergonomics examples (pseudo-code):
- SessionBuilder.create().onParcel(p => {
    if (p.type === 'action') renderActionPreview(p.payload);
}).onCommit((p) => {
    return sdk.ackParcel(p.id, {ack:true});
}).start();

Tradeoffs and open questions:
- Cost model: tentative parcels consume runtime unless server aggressively prunes uncommitted state. We need a token billing model that favors commits and charges lower for purely speculative partials.
- Complexity for simple apps: small apps may prefer a single streaming string; parcels add cognitive overhead. Consider opt-in via a response_mode parameter.
- Ordering and causal guarantees: parcels are ordered within a session but parallel backfilled tool results may reorder semantics. We experimented with causal tags (causal_parent_id) but the SDK surface got complex.
- Safety and privacy: tentative parcels that contain PII and trigger tool calls are riskier. Need server-side controls to block accidental tool invocation until commit on enterprise tenants.

Operational considerations:
- Telemetry: we log parcel lifecycle events (emitted, acked, nacked, committed, expired) with sampling. Implement trace-id per parcel for cross-service correlation.
- Retention: tentative parcel state TTL (default 60s) vs committed (retention per tenant policy).
- Rollouts: feature gated behind response_mode=parcelled and behind an account flag for early adopters.

Experiment log (lab runs):
- 2024-10-12: prototype over WebSocket, SessionBuilder MVP. Observed 2x fewer network events for multi-tool flows vs naive tool-per-token approach.
- 2024-10-24: mobile stress test (iPhone 12): UI flood reduced by 70% with size_hint pacing; battery impact minimal.
- 2024-11-02: customer sandbox (internal CS team): positive feedback for preview+commit semantics; confusion around pricing expectations.

Proposed API defaults (recommendation):
- response_mode default: "stream" (backwards compatible). 
- response_mode="parcelled" -> parcels emitted; SDKs expose high-level SessionBuilder.
- TTL: tentative parcels expire after 30s unless client requests extension.
- Billing: charge tokens for emitted parcels; additional small commit fee for finalization in Hosted billing (experiment).

Open work / TODOs:
- [ ] Design exact proto for parcel metadata (confidence, causal tags, tool-hint format).
- [ ] Billing alignment: coordinate with finance on tentative vs committed billing signals.
- [ ] Security policy: admin controls to disable auto-tool-invoke on tentative.
- [ ] SDK templates: JS, Swift, Kotlin high-level builders and migration guide.
- [ ] UX patterns doc: sample UI flows for preview+commit, rollback, and local edits.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally rough. The intent is to capture a developer-ergonomic approach to incremental, commit-able streaming without presuming we must replace the existing streaming model. Think of parcels as an additive surface for applications that need discrete side-effects tied to parts of the response.
- Some implementation sketches are naive — the goal is to get product alignment before handing to serving-runtime and infra for feasibility/benchmarks.

Appendix: small glossary
- Parcel: independent output unit.
- Tentative: not durable; intended for preview/speculative side-effects.
- Committed: durable, persisted, signals successful completion of an action.
- SessionBuilder: high-level client API for parcel flows.

Quick links (internal):
- Prototype repo: github.com/redwood-inference/parcelled-stream-proto (internal)
- Notes from mobile lab: /internal/mobile/parcel-lab-2024-10

End of doc.
